issues.legal_issue: An unmarried daughter may obtain an enhanced share under a statutory change to coparcenary rights in pending final-decree proceedings in a partition suit where the property has not yet been partitioned, notwithstanding that the preliminary decree has become final as to the shares it determined.
material_facts: A partition suit resulted in a preliminary decree determining the parties’ shares, and that decree was affirmed on appeal.
When the statutory amendment granting daughters coparcenary rights came into force, final-decree proceedings were pending and the property had not been divided by metes and bounds.
The daughter was unmarried when the amendment came into force and sought an equal share in the pending final-decree proceedings.
The application was rejected on the grounds that the preliminary decree had become final and the amendment could not be applied in the final-decree proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The daughter could claim the enhanced share in the pending final-decree proceedings. The application was allowed, and the final decree was to be made or amended to give effect to her right.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 6A of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, inserted by the Hindu Succession (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 1990, an unmarried daughter acquired coparcenary rights equal to those of a son. Articles 14, 15(1) and 15(3) of the Constitution support giving effect to the amendment’s equality-enhancing purpose. A partition suit proceeds in stages: a preliminary decree is conclusive as to the matters it decides, but the suit is not fully and completely decided until the final decree. Under Phoolchand v. Gopal Lal and S. Sai Reddy v. S. Narayana Reddy, a court may vary shares or pass a further preliminary decree in a partition suit when an intervening event changes the parties’ rights before final partition. Venkata Reddy v. Pethi Reddy and Gyarsi Bai v. Dhansukh Lal concern the finality of matters decided in a preliminary decree and do not prevent giving effect to a later statutory change in a pending partition suit; Mool Chand v. Deputy Director, Consolidation does not establish otherwise. The court also relied on the absence of a bar under the Code of Civil Procedure to varying shares in this situation and allowed relief under Sections 151, 152 and 153 CPC.

rule.if: partition_suit and preliminary_decree_passed and partition_not_completed and final_decree_proceedings_pending_when_law_changed and law_change_grants_daughters_coparcenary_rights and daughter_unmarried_when_law_changed

predicates.partition_suit: A party brought a suit seeking partition of joint family property.
predicates.preliminary_decree_passed: The court passed a preliminary decree specifying the parties’ shares.
predicates.partition_not_completed: The property had not been divided by metes and bounds among the parties.
predicates.final_decree_proceedings_pending_when_la: Final-decree proceedings were pending when the change in the governing law took effect.
predicates.law_change_grants_daughters_coparcenary_: The legislature changed the governing law to grant daughters coparcenary rights equal to those of sons.
predicates.daughter_unmarried_when_law_changed: The daughter whose share is claimed was unmarried when the change in law took effect.
predicates.daughter_entitled_to_equal_share_in_fina: The daughter is entitled to an equal share to be given effect in the final decree.

issues.definition: When a partition suit has a preliminary decree but the property remains undivided, a qualifying change in law taking effect while final-decree proceedings are pending permits an unmarried daughter covered by that change to receive an equal share in the final decree.
